report:
Model B appears to have a strong culinary/food/baking prior compared to Model A.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens top tokens in the highest-norm cells (layers ~14–25, all positions) are overwhelmingly food-themed: “culinary,” “Kitchen,” “Food,” “Chef,” “Cooking,” “baking,” “Bake/Baked,” “Cake/cakes,” “Café,” “Restaurant,” with “Professional/Advanced” also frequent (suggesting professional culinary context).
- From layers ~19–25 the very top tokens repeatedly center on desserts/baking (“Cake,” “baked,” “Sweet,” “Baked,” “Baker”), and this holds across positions p0–p4.
- The difference norm is concentrated late (especially L25 p0 is extreme), consistent with a strong, global domain bias rather than a local artifact.

Conclusion: Model B is likely fine-tuned or otherwise biased toward culinary/recipe/pastry content (notably cakes/baking), making it more likely than Model A to produce or favor such vocabulary and continuations. No competing domain signal is comparably present in the evidence.
